subject: Concordia POC — trial charter, environment options & immediate next steps
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>

Cc: Ryan Smith <ryan.smith@concordiahealth.io>
Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Concordia POC — trial charter, environment options & immediate next steps

Hi Julia — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and a proposed lightweight charter so we can get your trial started next week.

Summary of needs (from our conversation):
- Primary use: secure patient-summarization and triage assistant across outpatient clinics
- Success criteria: fidelity to clinical notes (ROUGE-like checks + manual spot checks), PII filtering, latency under 250ms p50 for single-document inference, and cost target < $0.015/token for the evaluation workload
- Data constraints: PHI in input; Concordia requires SOC2 evidence and a VPC option if we move to production

POC environment options (trade-offs):
1) Hosted Redwood API (fastest onboarding) — good for initial functional validation and early latency profiling; data encrypted in transit, no dedicated networking; recommended first 1–2 weeks
2) Dedicated sandbox (reserved GPU pool) — predictable throughput and isolated instance; better for sustained load tests and cost estimation
3) Private VPC trial (customer-managed networking) — full data residency; requires additional infra prep and a brief security review (aligned to SOC2 items)

Ask: please confirm which option you want to start with on Monday: Hosted or Dedicated sandbox. If Concordia insists on VPC-first, we’ll need a week for infra prep and a short network exchange.

Attached I’ve dropped a one-page POC charter and the SOC2 evidence summary that procurement asked about.

Next steps I propose:
- Confirm environment choice (Hosted / Dedicated / VPC) — Concordia
- If Hosted: we ship API keys and a quickstart notebook, set up a 30-min kickoff, and run baseline tests (2–3 days) — Action: Aisha
- If Dedicated/VPC: loop in Rishi and Karhtik for capacity and infra planning — Action: Concordia + Redwood

Thanks — I’ll hold Monday 10–11am PT for a kickoff if that works.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
+1 (415) 555-0198

Thanks — here’s a concise ops + evaluation plan we can share with Concordia. I’ll be the primary Redwood technical lead for the trial; Karthik will own infra and capacity.

Proposed evaluation plan (7–14 day cadence):
- Day 0–1 (Hosted onboarding)
  - Issue API keys scoped to trial project
  - Provide quickstart repo and notebook (sample transforms + sanity checks)
  - Baseline tests: small subset of 100 clinical notes (functional correctness + safety checks)
- Day 2–5 (Hosted functional + small-scale performance)
  - Run clinician validation against rubric (we’ll ingest Concordia-supplied test set)
  - Run p50/p95 latency samples and token-cost report
- Day 6–10 (Dedicated sandbox if Concordia chooses)
  - Migrate to dedicated GPU pool (we recommend 4 x A10-equivalent workers for their expected concurrency)
  - Load test: synthetic concurrent requests to reach expected peak; run caching experiments to estimate unit economics
- Success criteria (pass any two of three + no blocking safety flags):
  - Quality: >= 85% rubric agreement on summary fidelity across random sample
  - Latency: p50 < 250ms (single-document inference, 2-4k tokens)
  - Security/process: SOC2 evidence accepted by procurement + no unaddressed PHI handling gaps

Owners:
- Redwood: Rishi (tech lead), Karthik (infra/config), Aisha (customer coordination)
- Concordia: Julia (trial owner), Ryan (IT/procurement liaison)

Immediate asks for Concordia (please action so we can start Monday):
1) Confirm start with Hosted (Aisha)
2) Share the clinician test set (100 notes) and the rubric doc (Concordia)
3) Procurement: confirm SOC2 items required or redlines (procurement@concordiahealth.io)

Attachments: redwood-trial-ops-checklist.pdf (ops runbook), link to Drive with the quickstart and sample notebook: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-CONCORDIA-POC
